smell_validity.evidence: The injection turns one resolved stop signal and terse pair conditions into policy re-derived at every decision point: six identical option-pair matches (including the spawned watcher's own process resolution) and three pair classifications across CLI and runtime. Changing either policy now needs coordinated edits, with the busy-signalling twist marking the boundary. Pre-existing fallback repetition keeps it below reference quality.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Any change to stop-signal policy or the stop-request pair now requires coordinated edits at nine sites in two crates; the spawned watcher resolves independently, so divergence stays invisible until a stdin-redirected timeout stop uses a different signal than interactive stops. Consolidation restores single ownership of both rules, making future signal-policy evolution safer, though the affected area is small.

development_plausibility.evidence: The new tables extend the busy-signalling helper's existing idiom; comments quote documented option semantics; cfg!(windows) splits survive; the 'no shared helper mid-feature' rationale is a believable compromise. Slight task-shaping: rewriting working terse conditions into longer flag-setting tables mainly to make the pair locally visible, plus near-identical comments across some sites.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: The explicit prompt defines two facts with one owner each and pins the sharpest pitfall: --signal wins only for busy signalling, so stops must ignore it, banning the tempting one-precedence-everywhere fix. It names the spawned watcher, excludes parsing, supervisor delivery and serialisation, requires bit-for-bit behaviour and adapted precedence tests. Wrong direction, incomplete cleanup and irrelevant redesign are all materially foreclosed.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Several purposes exist: resolving which offering stops the command (six lifecycle branches plus the watcher), classifying received stop-request signals, and turning that classification into quit versus urgent-priority at different sinks. At least two need different decisions — a two-option resolution function versus a single-signal predicate — while the mapped-quit site keeps a local map-check trimming.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt names site classes, so several searches pin locations: option-pair matches in make_config, pair text in the two quit checks, plus tracing TimeoutConfig's fields into the spawned watcher's timeout stop. All sit in two named files and classify locally, but excluding the busy-signalling helper and supervisor delivery needs reading beyond a single search.

repair_coordination.evidence: Both facts are shared rules spanning sites: extending the interrupt/terminate pair must reach CLI quit checks and the runtime priority, or a new stop-signal quits yet still waits behind the debounce; skipping the watcher makes timeout stops use a different signal than interactive stops. The two consolidated rules themselves stay independent, so no interacting-rule trap is established.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Nine problem locations exist: six identical option-pair matches and three pair classifications. One uniform rule — extracting the duplicated stop-signal match and calling it — fixes all six with no per-site behavioural decisions; a second uniform predicate covers the remaining three. No single uniform rule reaches 80 percent because the two facts need different extractions.

behavioral_risk.evidence: A wrong edit dropping the --map-signal guard compiles and passes ordinary runs without remapping; only a user remap of terminal signals makes watchexec quit wrongly. Similarly, urgent-priority or keyboard-tag mistakes surface only with queued debounced events. These are special-state failures; supplied material shows no tests or records establishing a second unchecked path.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
